 By 
 Juan Pablo Aravena
 in
 NBA Basketball
 Published:
 November 4, 2026 at 7:14 pm EST
 Oct 31, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) looks up in the second half against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images 
 Mavericks vs Spurs will be one of the standout games in the NBA schedule on Wednesday
 Cooper Flagg , Victor Wembanyama and De’Aaron Fox are attractive options for Mavericks vs Spurs player props
 Read on to find my top Mavericks vs Spurs picks , player props and best bets
 The San Antonio Spurs (5-2 SU, 3-4 ATS, 2-5 O/U) host the Dallas Mavericks (4-3 SU, 4-3 ATS, 2-5 O/U) at the Frost Bank Center on November 4, 2026, for a 9:30 PM ET tip-off on ESPN. This Lone Star clash highlights a clash in styles, matching Dallas’ top-heavy offensive usage against San Antonio’s stifling half-court defense anchored by Victor Wembanyama.
 Sitting as heavy 12.5-point home favorites with the total set at 226.5 points, oddsmakers anticipate the Spurs dictating tempo while the Mavericks fight from behind. Leveraging early-season home-road splits and market disparities, here are my three favorite player prop picks for tonight’s matchup.
 Mavericks vs Spurs Player Prop Picks
 The NBA player props market for this prime-time contest offers compelling value when I target the contrasting offensive philosophies of these rosters. Given the inflated total pointing to extra possessions, I am keying in on usage-heavy focal points and distinct defensive vulnerabilities to extract value.
 Mavericks vs Spurs Prop Pick #1: Cooper Flagg 25+ Points (-108, Novig)
 Despite facing a stout Spurs defense allowing just 108.3 points per game and boasting a 106.8 defensive rating, backing Cooper Flagg’s immense volume remains a sharp angle. Flagg averages 25.2 points overall and 25.0 points in away games, fueled by a massive 31.3% usage rate on the road.
 Flagg has already proven capable of handling heavy scoring responsibility, clearing 25 points in four of his six appearances this season – delivering outputs of 32 at Houston, 29 at Miami, 26 against Oklahoma City, and 33 versus the Rockets on October 30. He averages 17.8 field goal attempts per game and logs 33.5 minutes as the focal engine of Dallas’ attack.
 When the contest tightens, the Mavericks lean heavily on their young star, as he averages 9.5 points in clutch situations. With guaranteed minutes and high-leverage shot attempts driving his floor, expect Flagg to eclipse his 24.5-point line in tonight’s NBA player points props , given a likely game script that requires constant offensive output.

 Mavericks vs Spurs Prop Pick #2: De’Aaron Fox 6+ Assists (-127, Kalshi)
 The Mavericks struggle to contain ball movement, surrendering 26.7 opponent assists per game, and De’Aaron Fox is perfectly equipped to exploit this perimeter weakness. The speedy guard orchestrates the Spurs’ offense brilliantly, averaging 6.4 assists in home games and identical numbers over his last 10 contests.
 Fox has dished out at least six assists in five of his seven games this season, recording counts of 7, 9, 9, 6, and 7 helpers. That includes a 9-assist gem on the road against this very Mavericks squad on Oct. 24. Boasting a stellar 13:5 assist-to-turnover in his home floor, Fox pushes the pace without squandering possessions.
 Given the Mavericks’ vulnerability to backcourt facilitators and Fox’s steady seasonal baseline, backing the over in the NBA player assist props provides a distinct edge.

 Mavericks vs Spurs Prop Pick #3: Victor Wembanyama Under 26.5 Points (+100, Novig)
 Fading a generational talent is never comfortable, but the underlying metrics indicate the Under is the savvy play for Victor Wembanyama at even money. While his 36.6% home usage rate is astronomical, Wembanyama’s scoring efficiency dips in his own building, where he averages 24.2 points on 44.2% shooting at home compared to his 25.7 overall season mark — and 29.5 points per game on the road.
 Wembanyama has remained under 26.5 points in four of his five home games at the Frost Bank Center this season, finishing with totals of 12, 25, 29, 43, and 12 points. He was also held to 23 points on 18 shots in his earlier meeting against Dallas on Oct. 24. The Mavericks carry a respectable 109.2 defensive rating and possess the interior size to challenge his 14.8 home points in the paint per game.
 Given these moderate home splits and volatile perimeter shooting nights, this inflated total sits slightly too high.
